messages:
liam: Seeing repeated OOMs on cluster-gpu-44 during a customer long-chat. 3 failures in 2 hours. KV cache memory jumps to 98% then OOMs. Logs show intense page churn + immediate re-access of evicted segments — looks like fragmentation + eviction thrash. Posting sample log: 
```
[2026-01-27T14:02:11Z] kvcache: evict segment id=0x7f3 size=48MB
[2026-01-27T14:02:11Z] kvcache: allocate segment id=0x8d2 size=48MB
[2026-01-27T14:02:11Z] attention: fetch kv for token_range=0-256
[2026-01-27T14:02:12Z] kvcache: page-in segment id=0x7f3 (hot)
OOM at 14:02:13
```
liam: This pattern repeats for long contexts (>16k tokens) with mixed user/system prompts. No obvious spike in request rate.
olivia: thanks for the dump. suspecting small-segment churn + LRU mismatch. fragmentation means free list contains many tiny fragments that are unusable for incoming large allocations.
maya: do we have memory histograms from the allocator around the time? also what's kernel selection doing for these requests (fp16 vs int8 paths)?
liam: allocator hist shows many ~1-8MB free blocks and lots of 48MB allocations failing. model is gptx-30b-32k quantized. kernels are choosing fused matmul for large seqs.
sam: infra noticed a slow down in background GC of the kvcache pager (pager thread starving). might be scheduling related on that node.
noah: runtime-oncall? any auto-fallback in place today? i thought we had a smaller-variant fallback.
runtime-oncall: current policy: fallback -> smaller model variant if overall mem pressure detected OR route to another region. but fallback only triggers when node is completely unhealthy; it doesn't handle transient eviction thrash.
olivia: short-term mitigations we can push now: 1) lower kvcache.page_threshold to force early page-out for large contiguous segments. 2) change eviction policy to segmented-LRU (prefer evicting cold subsegments rather than entire segments). 3) add per-request "no-kv" fallback header so we can retry without using KV for a retry attempt. 4) return 503+Retry-After when node is >95% and enable client-side jittered retry. example config diff:
```
kvcache:
  eviction_policy: segmented_lru
  page_threshold: 0.75  # page earlier
  min_segment_size: 16MB
runtime:
  request_fallback_headers:
    - X-Redwood-NoKV
```
maya: +1 to no-kv header. need to test quality/regression on long contexts though — might increase token cost but avoids OOM.
sam: infra can bump pager thread niceness / pin it to cpu to avoid starvation. also can set vm.swappiness-like knob for our pager.
olivia: longer-term: 1) compacting allocator pass to coalesce small fragments during idle windows. 2) change segment allocation to prefer contiguous runs (reduce fragmentation). 3) implement a kv-rescue mode: if we detect repeated evict+page-in of same segment within X seconds, mark segment as "hot-pinned" and allocate emergency reserve to avoid thrash. 4) expose memory pressure metric to routing to prefer lower-latency nodes with headroom.
liam: can we implement no-kv retry logic in the API gateway quickly? on failure, gateway should do a single immediate retry with `X-Redwood-NoKV: 1` then if still failing return 503 with Retry-After. also log shard id and kv stats.
sam: can do. will add gateway flag and metric. rollout can be a gradual canary.
noah: do we want an automatic silent degrade path (downgrade to 8k context) for in-flight sessions? that could be surprising.
olivia: we should avoid silent change to user-visible context size. prefer explicit fallback model or no-kv. silent context trimming only if user provided 'allow_truncation=true'.
liam: experiment idea: implement small reactive reserve: keep a 128MB emergency buffer per node that is only consumed when pager detects thrash; would avoid immediate OOMs while we decide fallback. pros/cons?
maya: reserve buys time but hides the underlying fragmentation. need compaction + allocator work still.
infra-bot: patch queued: "gateway: add no-kv retry header" pr#4123 — will run e2e. scheduled canary 10% tomorrow.
olivia: next steps: 1) sam: pin pager thread + vm knobs (today). 2) infra-bot: deploy gateway retry (tomorrow canary). 3) maya/olivia: prototype segmented_lru & reserve simulation (this week). 4) liam: collect allocator hist + per-segment reuse pattern and attach to incident ticket. 5) runtime-oncall: update oncall runbook to recommend retry-without-kv and return 503+Retry-After when >95% memory.
liam: assigning myself to gather more logs and produce minimal repro. thanks all. :thumbsup:
